clue.text: Stone bloke found inscribed with a note

indicators.note: something inscribed with words has them written into it, so the word for bloke takes the note phrase inside it

parts.note: a bloke is a man, a male
a chit is a short written note or voucher

explanation.surface: A man's name has been found carved into a stone along with a short message.
explanation.definitionFit: Malachite is a green copper mineral, polished as an ornamental stone.

clue.text: Legend behind uprising needing no introduction

indicators.note: in a down entry an uprising reads from the bottom upwards, turning the letters round
needing no introduction loses the opening letter of the word for behind

parts.note: a behind is a bottom, the buttocks

explanation.surface: A famous figure needs no introduction, being behind a popular revolt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'needing no introduction' drops B from BOTTOM to give OTTOM, which 'uprising' turns round.
explanation.definitionFit: A legend can be an inscription or a short slogan on a crest, as a motto is.

clue.text: Little room on raised platform for more bananas

parts.note: the loo is the smallest room, the toilet
a pier is a raised walkway or platform built out over water

explanation.surface: A small shed perched on a raised stage holds extra bananas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bananas' is slang for crazy, and 'more bananas' wants a comparative of that.
explanation.definitionFit: Bananas and loopy are both slang for crazy, so the comparative forms match.

clue.text: Companion suffering nip

parts.note: CH stands for Companion of Honour, a British order
someone suffering is ill

explanation.surface: A friend is suffering a pinch or bite.
explanation.definitionFit: A nip in the air is a sharp coldness, a light coolness.

clue.text: Deceit conjured up over a drink

indicators.note: conjured up as by a magician's trickery, the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A trickster's sleight of hand produces a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Iced tea is a cold beverage of chilled tea.

clue.text: Point-to-point on horse for young hunter's quarry?

parts.note: east is a point of the compass
E is the abbreviation for east, another compass point
re means on, concerning
gee-gee is a child's word for a horse

explanation.surface: A cross-country horse race seems to be what a young rider is chasing.
explanation.walkthrough: A point-to-point is a British amateur horse race over fences, which steers the solver away from compass points. 'for young' marks GG as nursery talk.
explanation.definitionFit: Children hunt for chocolate eggs hidden at Easter, so these are their quarry.

clue.text: Turn pipe down well!

parts.note: a turn in a game is a go
to pipe down is to hush, the order sh

explanation.surface: Someone is told to turn the music down, and replies with surprise.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are mild exclamations of surprise, interchangeable interjections.

clue.text: Currency banked by doctor, a relative

indicators.note: banked by means bordered on each side, so the doctor letters flank the currency

parts.note: a GP is a general practitioner, a family doctor
the rand is South Africa's currency

explanation.surface: A doctor puts money in the bank on behalf of a family member.
explanation.definitionFit: A grandfather is a family member, a kinsman.

clue.text: Club that may follow club, loosely speaking?

indicators.note: loosely speaking says the word is said aloud approximately rather than exactly

parts.note: a club sandwich is a stacked sandwich, so this word follows club

explanation.surface: Wonders what might come after a club, in a casual sense.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'Club' is the golf club; the second is the club sandwich.
explanation.definitionFit: A sand wedge is a golf iron for getting out of bunkers.

clue.text: A suspicious protein for poisoner

indicators.note: suspicious suggests something fishy or not straight, so the letters of the following word are rearranged

explanation.surface: A dodgy protein found in the system points the finger at a poisoner.
explanation.definitionFit: Atropine, from deadly nightshade, is a toxic alkaloid, an agent that poisons.

clue.text: Jammy and eggy?

definitions.meaning: British slang for lucky, flukily fortunate
eggy in the sense of full of eggs, as frogspawn is

explanation.surface: Two breakfast spreads described: one with jam, one with egg.
explanation.walkthrough: JAMMY is everyday British slang for lucky; the question mark flags the playful second sense, where spawn means fish or frog eggs.
explanation.definitionFit: Spawny is British slang for lucky, and literally means having or like spawn, the eggs of fish and frogs.

clue.text: In which one fuels spreading of cod malaise?

definitions.text: In which one fuels spreading of cod malaise?

indicators.note: one fuels the mixture by being fed into it, so the letter for one goes inside
spreading scatters the letters of the words that follow into a new order

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: Asks which place lets each of us feed a general gloom about trivia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fuels' puts I inside an anagram of COD MALAISE; the whole clue also describes online platforms where users spread low-grade malaise.
explanation.definitionFit: Online platforms like Twitter are where each user can stoke and spread a general mood of discontent.

clue.text: Current broadcast not working, so restricted

indicators.note: broadcast means spoken out over the air, so the word is taken as heard

parts.note: a tide is a current of the sea
a computer system that is not working is down

explanation.surface: A radio broadcast is off air, leaving listeners cut off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast' is the sound signal here, not an anagram: TIDE spoken is TIED.
explanation.definitionFit: Tied down describes someone constrained by obligations, held back.

clue.text: Wife escaping winding of twister, as bricks falling?

indicators.note: escaping says the wife letter gets out of the word that follows
winding twists the letters of the word that follows into a new order

explanation.surface: A wife runs from a tornado as bricks rain down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'escaping' removes W from TWISTER and 'winding of' rearranges the remaining TISTER.
explanation.definitionFit: Tetris is the video game in which falling block shapes must be fitted into rows, so bricks falling describes it.

clue.text: Author's fictional land inspired by drink, something juicy written up

indicators.note: in a down entry, written up means set down from bottom to top, in reverse
something inspired by is breathed in, so the land goes inside the drink

parts.note: ale is a drink, beer
Oz is the fictional land of the Wizard of Oz
a lime is a juicy citrus fruit

explanation.surface: An author's imaginary realm was inspired by a drink and something juicy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inspired by' wants to mean creative influence; here it means breathed in, so OZ goes inside. OZ is the land of The Wizard of Oz.
explanation.definitionFit: Emile Zola was the French novelist of the Rougon-Macquart cycle.

clue.text: Do say that which has been identified repeatedly in rant

indicators.note: in places the doubled pronoun inside the word for rant

parts.note: to spout is to rant, holding forth

indicators.note: repeatedly says the pronoun appears more than once, here twice

parts.note: it is the pronoun for a thing already identified

explanation.surface: Someone is urged to speak up about what has been named again and again in a tirade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Do say' is an imperative: please speak.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom urges someone hesitant to tell what they are holding back.

clue.text: Queen saying poisoner behaved like a chicken

indicators.note: saying means spoken out, so the phrase counts as it sounds

parts.note: an adder is a venomous snake, a poisoner, and a hen behaving like a chicken has laid an egg

explanation.surface: A queen remarks that a poisoner was a coward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'behaved like a chicken' wants to mean acted cowardly; it is a hen producing an egg.
explanation.definitionFit: Adelaide was a British queen consort, wife of William IV.

clue.text: Like to insert tongue, opening wide

indicators.note: to insert means put inside, so the language goes into the word for like

parts.note: to dig something is slang for liking it
a tongue is a language, here Latin

explanation.surface: Someone enjoys a French kiss, opening wide.
explanation.definitionFit: Dilating means widening or expanding, as a pupil enlarges.

clue.text: Queen snubbed by lay reader unfortunately before

indicators.note: snubbed by means pushed out by, so the queen's letters are rejected from the rest
unfortunately suggests things gone awry, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen

explanation.surface: A church lay reader gave the Queen the cold shoulder earlier on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'snubbed by' removes ER from LAY READER and 'unfortunately' rearranges what is left, LAYADR.
explanation.definitionFit: Already means by this time, previously.

clue.text: Water supply in blood, lose it!

indicators.note: in puts the water source inside the word for blood

parts.note: gore is spilt blood
a spa is a mineral spring, a supply of water

explanation.surface: A water supply contaminated with blood prompts a furious outburst.
explanation.definitionFit: Go spare is British slang for becoming furious, which is what losing one's temper means.

clue.text: Dogsbody, an active digger

definitions.meaning: a lowly helper who runs errands, a gofer, which can also be spelt this way
a burrowing rodent of North America that tunnels busily

explanation.surface: Describes a hard-working junior who will dig in at anything.
explanation.definitionFit: A gopher is a burrowing rodent and, as a variant spelling of gofer, an errand-runner.

clue.text: Beautiful and delicate creature: Mona Lisa, perhaps

definitions.meaning: a pretty butterfly, orange and black, of that name
a woman depicted in oils, as Leonardo's sitter is

explanation.surface: The Mona Lisa as a beautiful, fragile figure.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a migratory butterfly and also literally a woman in a painting, such as the Mona Lisa.

clue.text: Part of one arm is stuck, almost a disaster

indicators.note: Part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone's arm gets caught in machinery and they barely escape catastrophe.
explanation.definitionFit: A near miss is an incident that came very close to being an accident.

clue.text: Italy yet to be beaten after second half

indicators.note: after places the Italy-and-yet part behind the word for second

parts.note: mo is short for moment, a second
I is the international vehicle code for Italy

indicators.note: beaten as eggs are, so the letters of the word are mixed up

explanation.surface: Italy are still to lose, playing in the second half of a match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'second half' looks like one phrase, but 'second' is wordplay and 'half' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A moiety is a formal word for one of two equal parts.

clue.text: See 10
Thinner sheep carrying fatter rump

indicators.note: carrying means holding within, so the sheep word takes the letter inside

parts.note: tups are rams, male sheep

indicators.note: a rump is the hind end, so the last letter of the word is taken

explanation.surface: A lean sheep carries a sheep with a bigger backside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Thinner' looks like a comparative adjective; it is paint thinner, a solvent.
explanation.definitionFit: Turps, short for turpentine, is a solvent used to dilute oil paint.

clue.text: Something red marked for attention of the chairman, last of post collected

parts.note: a letter marked for someone's attention is addressed to them

indicators.note: collected means gathered in, so the chairman takes the letter inside

parts.note: Mao Zedong was known as Chairman Mao

indicators.note: last of picks the final letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: A red document marked for the chairman's attention arrives with the last post.
explanation.definitionFit: A ripe tomato is a familiar red fruit, so it is one example of a red thing.

clue.text: Car blue, in one sense?

parts.note: an Audi is a German make of car
blue is the colour of the British Conservatives, so a blue is a Tory

explanation.surface: Asks whether a car is blue in some sense.
explanation.walkthrough: TORY: a member of Britain's Conservative Party, whose colour is blue.
explanation.definitionFit: Auditory means relating to hearing, which is one of the five senses.

clue.text: See 20
Those in opposition named jerks, accordingly on the periphery

indicators.note: on the periphery says the word for accordingly sits around the outside of the rest

parts.note: thus means accordingly, consequently

indicators.note: jerks means twitches sharply, jolting the letters of the word into a new order

explanation.surface: Opponents name a group of jerks, who end up on the fringes.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase sets two opposed camps against each other, our side versus theirs.
